report:
Native liver, total hepatectomy

Received fresh is a native liver weighing 1150 g and measuring 22 x 15 x 10 cm. The hilar margins (bile duct, portal vein and hepatic artery) are submitted en face. Thrombus is present in the portal vein, occluding the main trunk, adherent to the wall. The gallbladder is attached (8 cm, wall 2 mm, no stones). Three hilar lymph nodes are identified. The liver is serially sliced at 5 mm intervals. The parenchyma is diffusely micronodular. No mass or prominent nodule is seen. All lesions described on imaging are identified. Representative sections are taken; see block key.

(1-2) Hilar margins en face.
(3) Portal vein thrombus.
(4-7) Background liver.
(8) Gallbladder.
(9) Hilar lymph nodes.

The liver shows established cirrhosis (Ishak stage 6/6) with mild interface and lobular activity. Ground-glass hepatocytes are present. The portal vein contains organising bland thrombus. Three hilar lymph nodes show reactive changes. The gallbladder shows chronic cholecystitis. There is no dysplasia or malignancy.

LIVER, native, total hepatectomy - CHRONIC HEPATITIS B with CIRRHOSIS (Ishak stage 6/6)
